body:
Related fact: open PR #1099 (#1071, ready and `merge-ready`) already makes this change in law (a). `crates/sim/src/verify/crossing.rs` gains `touching()`: a chord end within `TOUCH` = 1e-9 mm of the other chord's line is read as on it, so no crossing, applied after `proper_cross`. That is the same tolerance as the planner's `guard::crosses` here. Found because the thread mill's retract (the ride reversed at feed) put shared joints a last bit apart and blocked the post.

Pinned there by `crates/sim/tests/crossing_retrace.rs`:
- `a_helix_run_back_over_its_own_trace_is_no_crossing`: rounding-apart shared joints and collinear overlaps; all-pairs and bucketed.
- `a_real_crossing_still_reads_as_one_at_any_angle`: 90 degrees down to 0.001 rad.

`crossing_buckets` (bucketed vs all-pairs) stays green, and the batch gate on that branch was green.

Not covered there: this issue's exact pin pair (a shared end 1e-12 mm apart gives no warning; a crossing a micron through still warns). #1099 is ready and takes no pushes, so I can add that pair as a small test-only PR once #1099 merges. When it does, this issue can then close with `Fixes #1129`.
